textbookText: 61. The distance between two points (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) in a plane is given by: A) √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²] B) (x₂−x₁) + (y₂−y₁) C) (x₂−x₁) × (y₂−y₁) D) √(x₂−x₁) + √(y₂−y₁)
62. The slope of a line passing through points (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is: A) (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁) B) (x₂−x₁)/(y₂−y₁) C) (y₂+y₁)/(x₂+x₁) D) (x₂−x₁) × (y₂−y₁)
63. Two lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are: A) Equal B) Negative reciprocals of each other C) Both equal to zero necessarily D) Product equal to 1
64. Two lines are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes equals: A) −1 B) 1 C) 0 D) Undefined always
65. The equation of a straight line in slope-intercept form is: A) y = mx + c, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept B) y = mx² + c C) x = my + c D) mx + ny = 0 only
66. The general equation of a circle with center (h,k) and radius r is: A) (x−h)² + (y−k)² = r² B) x² + y² = r² (centered at origin only, regardless of h,k) C) (x−h) + (y−k) = r D) x² − y² = r²
67. The standard equation of a parabola with vertex at origin, opening rightward, is: A) y² = 4ax B) x² = 4ay C) x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 D) x² − y² = a²
68. The standard equation of an ellipse centered at the origin is: A) x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 B) y² = 4ax C) x² − y² = a² D) x²/a² − y²/b² = 1
69. The standard equation of a hyperbola centered at the origin (transverse axis along x) is: A) x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 B) x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 C) y² = 4ax D) x² + y² = a²
70. The eccentricity of a circle is always: A) 0 B) 1 C) Greater than 1 D) Undefined
71. The eccentricity of a parabola is always: A) Exactly 1 B) 0 C) Between 0 and 1 D) Greater than 1
72. For an ellipse, the eccentricity e satisfies: A) 0 < e < 1 B) e = 1 exactly C) e > 1 D) e = 0 exactly, same as a circle
73. For a hyperbola, the eccentricity e satisfies: A) e > 1 B) 0 < e < 1 C) e = 1 D) e = 0

74. The focus-directrix property defines a conic section as the locus of points where the ratio of distance from a fixed point (focus) to distance from a fixed line (directrix) equals: A) The eccentricity (a constant) B) Always exactly 1, for every conic C) Zero D) The radius of the conic

75. An extraordinary real-world application of conic sections is that: A) Planetary orbits follow elliptical paths, as described by Kepler's laws, with the sun at one focus B) Conic sections have no application outside pure mathematics C) All orbits in the solar system are perfect circles, never ellipses D) Parabolas are only used in abstract geometry, never in engineering (e.g., satellite dishes)
76. The midpoint of a line segment joining (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is: A) ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2) B) (x₁+x₂, y₁+y₂) C) ((x₁−x₂)/2, (y₁−y₂)/2) D) (x₁x₂, y₁y₂)
77. The angle between two straight lines with slopes m₁ and m₂ is given by: A) tan θ = |(m₁−m₂)/(1+m₁m₂)| B) tan θ = m₁ + m₂ C) tan θ = m₁ × m₂ D) tan θ = (m₁+m₂)/(1−m₁m₂)
78. The perpendicular distance from a point (x₁,y₁) to the line ax+by+c=0 is given by: A) |ax₁+by₁+c| / √(a²+b²) B) (ax₁+by₁+c) / (a+b) C) |ax₁+by₁+c| D) √(a²+b²) / |ax₁+by₁+c|

79. A parabola's "latus rectum" refers to: A) The chord through the focus, perpendicular to the axis of the parabola, with length 4a B) The vertex of the parabola C) The directrix of the parabola D) The eccentricity of the parabola
80. For an ellipse with semi-major axis a and semi-minor axis b (a > b), the relationship with focal distance c is: A) c² = a² − b² B) c² = a² + b² C) c = a × b D) c² = b² − a²

81. The equation x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 represents a circle with center: A) (−g, −f) and radius √(g²+f²−c) B) (g, f) and radius √(g²+f²+c) C) (0,0) always regardless of g, f, c D) (−g, f) and radius c

82. Which of these correctly describes an "asymptote" of a hyperbola? A) A straight line that the hyperbola approaches but never touches as it extends to infinity B) A line that always passes through the vertex of the hyperbola C) A line perpendicular to the transverse axis at the center D) The directrix of the hyperbola

83. Two straight lines are coincident (the same line) when: A) Their coefficients are proportional, including the constant term (a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂) B) Their slopes are negative reciprocals C) They intersect at exactly one point only D) They are always parallel but distinct

84. The condition for three points to be collinear (lying on a straight line) can be checked using: A) The area of the triangle formed by the three points being equal to zero B) Their sum being equal to zero C) Their product being a whole number D) Their distances from the origin being equal

85. In the equation of a circle, if the coefficients of x² and y² are unequal, the equation: A) Does NOT represent a circle B) Always represents a circle regardless of the coefficients C) Represents a circle only if they are both zero D) Represents a parabola instead of failing to be a circle (distractor mislabel)
